answer: The comet test I would run is Proof of unique crates.io publish history: crates published and downloaded over years, so each new name must bring its own proof instead of reusing a sibling's. The verifier never sees the raw secret, only a proof that crates published and downloaded over years — so privacy survives, and the ferrous is that a stolen database buys the attacker nothing at all. A farm could afford one proof, maybe ten, but the prism of a hundred is measured in weeks of work and thousands in fees, against a reward that shrinks per head.
